quotes.text: Here's a hard truth that most organizations learn the hard way. The only good backup is one you've actually restored and validated.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: States the core lesson of the episode: untested backups provide no real assurance.

quotes.text: A backup strategy without a restore test is just an expensive hope. You're paying for protection, you haven't confirmed works.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A memorable one-line argument for regular restore drills.

quotes.text: Once you set a retention period for a backup, that recovery point cannot be deleted early. Not by an administrator, not by someone who compromises an admin account.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains clearly why immutability protects backups even against compromised admins.

quotes.text: In a real ransomware attack, attackers almost always try to delete backups first. That's their playbook. Immutability stops that.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Connects attacker behavior directly to the defensive feature that counters it.

quotes.text: If your workloads are primarily in Azure, start with Azure backup. It's simple, cost-effective, and deeply integrated.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Gives a concrete, actionable recommendation for choosing a backup tool.

takeaways: Azure Backup is a managed platform that protects Azure VMs, SQL Server and SAP HANA databases, file shares, blobs, disks and on-premises servers from one vault, driven by policies.
Encryption, soft delete, immutability, multi-user authorization and Defender for Cloud malware scanning make backups hard for ransomware attackers to destroy or poison.
A backup is only proven once it has been restored, so schedule regular restore drills and review retention policies to avoid paying for recovery points you never need.
hook: Losing a server or VM to failure or ransomware is every IT team's nightmare, and tape-era backups only proved themselves when you tried to restore. This episode explains Azure Backup for IT admins and cloud beginners: what it protects, how snapshots and vaults work, how it resists attacks, what it costs, and why you must test your restores.
